clue.text: Insurance cost added to restaurant bill

parts.note: insurance is cover against loss or damage
a charge is the price or cost of something

explanation.surface: An insurance premium has somehow been tacked onto a diner's bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A cover charge is a fixed fee per head that some restaurants add to the bill.

clue.text: Incinerate the container that carried me back

indicators.note: a container that carries something holds it within, so the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: a crate is a wooden container for goods

indicators.note: back tells us the word me is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone vows to burn the box that brought them home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ME around; 'that carried' looks like a relative clause about a coffin but signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To incinerate a body is to cremate it, burning it to ashes.

clue.text: See nothing on the recorder

parts.note: vide is Latin for 'see', used in references
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone checks a recorder and finds nothing on it.
explanation.walkthrough: VIDE ('see', as in footnote references) sits on top of O in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A video is short for a video recorder, a machine that tapes television.

clue.text: Abstruse edict Nero issued anew

indicators.note: something reissued in a new form has its letters put out in a fresh order

explanation.surface: The emperor Nero reissues an obscure decree.
explanation.definitionFit: Recondite knowledge is obscure, hard to grasp, like something abstruse.

clue.text: Woman ensnares a man who'll succeed

indicators.note: to ensnare is to trap something within, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: her is a pronoun for a woman
a means one, the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A woman traps a man who is going to inherit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' stands for one, written as the Roman numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: An heir is the person in line to succeed to a title or estate.

clue.text: No point in chorister using declamatory language

indicators.note: using is a loose signal that the remaining letters are put to work in a new order
no here says the following letter is taken away from the chorister

parts.note: S is south, a compass point

explanation.surface: A choirboy performs with no hint of grand speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' removes S (a compass point) from CHORISTER, leaving CHORITER, which 'using' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhetoric is the art of persuasive or showy speech, language meant to impress.

clue.text: Once a court? Quite right

parts.note: ex means former, once

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a place was formerly a court and is told yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact means precise, accurate, perfectly correct.

clue.text: Pop means to torment many in church

indicators.note: in places the torment and many inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
to rack is to torment, as on the rack
L is the Roman numeral fifty, many

explanation.surface: Popular meaning to torment crowds in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' looks like a father or fizzy drink; it is the sound. L is the Roman fifty, standing for many.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackle is a snapping noise, like a pop.

clue.text: Manage to maintain good relations

explanation.surface: Instructions on how to cope and stay friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: To get along is to cope or manage; it also means to be friendly with others.

clue.text: Glandular trouble diner once exhibited

indicators.note: trouble suggests disorder, so these letters are disturbed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A diner once showed signs of a gland problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' looks like part of a medical phrase with 'Glandular' but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The endocrine system is made of glands secreting hormones into the blood.

clue.text: A centre of conflict

parts.note: a place where battles or contests take place, such as a stadium or field of struggle

explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a place of combat or competition, like a Roman amphitheatre.

clue.text: About to get a ring

parts.note: a round is a circle or ring

explanation.surface: Someone is about to receive a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' looks like 'on the point of'; 'About' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Around and about both mean approximately or on all sides.

clue.text: Frank must send letter to another chap

parts.note: to post is to send a letter by mail
Mark is a man's name, a chap

explanation.surface: Someone named Frank needs to write to another fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a man's name, but it is the verb meaning to stamp mail.
explanation.definitionFit: To frank mail is to stamp it with a mark showing postage paid.

clue.text: All the others in ancient Rome

definitions.text: All the others in ancient Rome

parts.words: All the others in ancient Rome
parts.note: a Latin phrase for 'and the rest', as a Roman would say it

explanation.definitionFit: Et alii is Latin for 'and others', abbreviated et al.

clue.text: Strange duet a lad praised excessively

indicators.note: strange signals the letters are made odd, rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd duet by a boy drew over-the-top praise.
explanation.definitionFit: To adulate someone is to flatter them with excessive admiration.

clue.text: Peg once used working dress

parts.note: a pin is a peg
afore is an old word for before, formerly or once

explanation.surface: A clothes peg once held up work clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: AFORE is an archaic word for 'before', so 'once'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinafore is a sleeveless apron or dress worn over clothes for work.

clue.text: Everyone high and dry?

parts.note: everyone means all
high means up, raised
with can stand for and, meaning together with

explanation.surface: Has everyone been left stranded?
explanation.walkthrough: Read as pieces, everyone, high and 'and' build the phrase; read whole, 'high and dry' means stranded, finished.
explanation.definitionFit: When it is all up with someone, they are finished, stranded beyond help.

clue.text: Low interest charge

parts.note: base means low or mean
a rate is a charge or price

explanation.surface: A loan's interest charge is pleasingly small.
explanation.walkthrough: The BASE RATE is the bank's benchmark interest rate.
explanation.definitionFit: A base rate is the central bank lending level that sets interest on loans.

clue.text: Reason and means to build elevated road

parts.note: a cause is a reason
a way is a means or method

explanation.surface: Engineers need motive and method to construct a raised road.
explanation.definitionFit: A causeway is a raised road across water or marsh.

clue.text: Expensive Italian accountants acquire capital!

parts.note: cara is Italian for dear, expensive
CA is a chartered accountant, so CAs are accountants

explanation.surface: Pricey Italian accountants take over a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: CARA is the Italian feminine form of 'dear'; CA is a Chartered Accountant.
explanation.definitionFit: Caracas is the capital city of Venezuela.

clue.text: Promise to provide soft illumination

parts.note: P is piano, soft in music
light is illumination

explanation.surface: Someone pledges to supply gentle lighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Promise' is the verb: to plight one's troth is to pledge it.
explanation.definitionFit: To plight is an old word meaning to pledge or vow.

clue.text: What people in the wrong suffer, perhaps

definitions.text: What people in the wrong suffer, perhaps

indicators.note: in puts the people inside the wrong

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
men are people

explanation.surface: Those in the wrong may end up suffering for it.
explanation.walkthrough: A tort is a civil wrong in law; the whole clue doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Torment is great suffering, the agony wrongdoers may endure.

clue.text: Landed properties in America create genuine obligations

parts.note: real means genuine
ties are bonds or obligations

explanation.surface: American estates create real duties for their owners.
explanation.definitionFit: Realty is the US term for real estate, land and buildings.

clue.text: Thanks secretaries for providing tasty snacks

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks
PA is a personal assistant, so PAs are secretaries

explanation.surface: Office staff are thanked for laying on nibbles.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is informal British 'thank you'; PA is a personal assistant.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapas are small Spanish savoury dishes served as snacks.

clue.text: Seem to take to the stage

explanation.surface: Looking as if one is about to perform.
explanation.definitionFit: To appear is to seem, and also to perform in a play or show.

clue.text: Boredom makes some proven nuisance even worse

indicators.note: some means only part of the words proven nuisance is taken

explanation.surface: Tedium makes a known pest even more irritating.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless weariness, a French word for tedium.

clue.text: Singular dessert made with common vegetable

parts.note: S abbreviates singular in grammar
pud is British slang for pudding, a dessert

explanation.surface: A one-off pudding made with a humble vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: PUD is short for pudding, the British word for a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Spud is a slang word for a potato.

clue.text: Move stealthily to spot fawn

explanation.surface: A hunter edges quietly forward to catch sight of a young deer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fawn' looks like a young deer, but it is the verb meaning to grovel.
explanation.definitionFit: To creep is to sneak quietly; it also means to toady, to be servile.

clue.text: Device needed to repair canal pipe

indicators.note: to repair is to put right, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A gadget is needed to fix a pipe by the canal.
explanation.definitionFit: An appliance is a device or machine, often for household use.

clue.text: Not one to buy with prudence

definitions.text: Not one to buy with prudence

parts.words: Not one to buy with prudence
parts.note: describes someone who purchases wildly, without care for saving money

explanation.definitionFit: A spendthrift is a wasteful person who spends money recklessly.
